name: Minimum Star Number
definition: For a finite binary class $\mathcal H$ and any (possibly unrealizable) labeling $g:\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}$, let $\mathrm S_g(\mathcal H)$ be the largest $d$ for which there are distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ and hypotheses $h_0,\ldots,h_d\in\mathcal H$ such that $h_0(x_j)=g(x_j)$ for all $j$, while $h_i(x_j)=g(x_j)$ holds exactly when $j\ne i$ for every $i\ge1$. The **minimum star number** is $\mathrm S_{\mathrm{min}}(\mathcal H)=\inf_g\mathrm S_g(\mathcal H)$.
graph_summary: Smallest star-number value over all possible centre labelings; it bounds a stable unlabeled compression scheme.
description: Hanneke's minimum-centred-star parameter. For finite binary classes it lies between VC dimension and the ordinary star number.

monotonic.proof: For every fixed centre labeling, every star of a subfamily remains a star after enlarging the class. Taking the infimum over centres preserves this inequality.
